items.title: Howard Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2025
items.q: I fell in love with the sound of the blues harmonica and all the Chicago guys, you know Paul Butterfield, James Cotton, Little Walter

ctx.x: Why did you not go in that direction with the chromatic harmonica?

Well the reason why I started playing the harmonica was that my buddies and I in high school and we started with the rock bands and then we started playing blues, and I fell in love with the sound of the blues harmonica and all the Chicago guys, you know Paul Butterfield, James Cotton, Little Walter – that sound. And you can’t get that sound on the chromatic. So you know once I discovered how to play chromatically on the diatonic harmonica I thought well why can’t I take this instrument into the same places that,…

myself how to play it in the early and mid-1970s when I was trying to get better at reading music on harmonica. Because I found it too difficult to read on this instrument while I was doing all of these manipulations with the inside of my mouth and all this stuff to get all the pitches. And gradually I became a very good reader on this. But yeah, this, the bluesy, soulfulness of this instrument, which is a total accident of design, is what appeals to me.
